issues.reason: The Existential section is explicit - with a verbal predicate "a/an" is a witness and "a verbal generic takes a bare plural or an explicit quantifier ... not 'a dog'", with the only carve-out reserved for modal predications - and the rule form additionally makes every keeper inherit the one shared sk_snuffer_1 and sk_station_1, which is false of the sentence.

"The direct-object roles are for objects the verb takes without a preposition": "the station" arrives via "with" and is neither an animate co-participant (CoAgent) nor the means (Instrument), so it belongs in the preposition-named oblique (With <event> sk_station_1), not in a second Theme on the inherit event.

gaps_confirmed: the with-phrase split names only CoAgent (an animate participant) and Instrument (the means), so an accompaniment "with" on an inanimate NP reaches the preposition-named oblique only by extension of the general "head is the preposition actually used" licence, with no explicit ruling

a frequency adverb ("often") over a witness-subject habitual: the QuantifierPhrase companion's first slot is a kind and the frequency strength is defined only on a rule or a flat generic, so the witness reading the Existential section mandates has no carrier for the adverb
defect_summary: Compliant subject form: a witness - (Member sk_keeper_1 keeper) plus an ordinary status-free (habitual) inherit event on that witness - never a kind-level Implication over (Member $x keeper); compliant with-phrase form: (With sk_inherit_1 sk_station_1) beside a single (Theme sk_inherit_1 sk_snuffer_1). Under that compliant subject route the instruction set licenses NO carrier for "often" - neither the frequency strength nor the QuantifierPhrase companion has a witness-scoped shape - so the adverb would have to be left out and the gap recorded (filed above).
notes: Granting the (unlicensed) rule route, the dial value 0.8 for "often" and the companion's kind/verb-lemma/word shape are right, and capitalized "Keeper" correctly stays a common noun with no Name atom.
